77977.subject: Technical Drawing
77977.question_text: List five essential drawing tools used in Technical Drawing and describe the specific function of each tool.
77977.explanation:
The five essential drawing tools and their functions are:

1. T-square: Used for drawing horizontal lines and as a guide for set squares.
2. Set squares (30°-60° and 45°): Used for drawing vertical and inclined lines at specific angles.
3. Compass: Used for drawing circles and arcs of various radii.
4. Protractor: Used for measuring and constructing angles.
5. French curve: Used for drawing smooth, irregular curves that are not circular.

77978.subject: Technical Drawing
77978.question_text: Which of the following is the largest standard drawing sheet size in the A-series?
77978.explanation: The A-series standard sheet sizes range from A0 (largest) to A8 (smallest). A0 has dimensions of $841 \text{ mm} \times 1189 \text{ mm}$ and is the largest in the series.

77979.subject: Technical Drawing
77979.question_text: Draw a standard title block for a Technical Drawing sheet and label five essential components that must be included in it.
77979.explanation:
A standard title block typically includes the following components:

1. Drawing title: Name of the drawing or project.
2. Drawing number: Unique identifier for the drawing.
3. Scale: The scale used in the drawing (e.g., 1:10).
4. Date: The date the drawing was completed.
5. Name of draughtsman/designer: Person responsible for the drawing.

The title block is usually located at the bottom right corner of the drawing sheet.

77980.subject: Technical Drawing
77980.question_text: Which line type is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
77980.explanation: A dashed line (also known as a hidden line) is used to represent edges or details that are not visible in the current view of an orthographic projection.

77981.subject: Technical Drawing
77981.question_text: Construct a perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB of length $80 \text{ mm}$ using only a compass and a straightedge. Show all construction lines clearly.
77981.explanation:
Steps to construct a perpendicular bisector:

1. Draw line segment AB of length $80 \text{ mm}$.
2. With A as the center, draw an arc with a radius greater than half of AB.
3. With B as the center, draw another arc of the same radius, intersecting the first arc at points C and D.
4. Draw a straight line through points C and D. This line is the perpendicular bisector of AB.

77982.subject: Technical Drawing
77982.question_text: Construct a regular hexagon with each side measuring $30 \text{ mm}$ using a compass and a straightedge. Show all construction lines.
77982.explanation:
Steps to construct a regular hexagon:

1. Draw a circle with radius $30 \text{ mm}$ (since the side of a regular hexagon equals the radius of its circumscribed circle).
2. Mark a point A on the circumference.
3. Using the same radius, step off points B, C, D, E, and F around the circumference.
4. Join the points A, B, C, D, E, and F to form the hexagon.

77983.subject: Technical Drawing
77983.question_text: Explain the difference between First Angle Projection and Third Angle Projection in orthographic drawing. Include a simple sketch to illustrate each method.
77983.explanation:
First Angle Projection:
The object is placed in the first quadrant, and the views are projected onto planes behind the object. The front view is placed below the top view.

Third Angle Projection:
The object is placed in the third quadrant, and the views are projected onto planes in front of the object. The front view is placed above the top view.

In both methods, the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view in First Angle and to the right in Third Angle.

77984.subject: Technical Drawing
77984.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the internal features of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it?
77984.explanation: A half section is used to show the internal features of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it, leaving the other half intact for external details.

77985.subject: Technical Drawing
77985.question_text: Draw an isometric view of a cube with each edge measuring $50 \text{ mm}$. Show all construction lines and label the isometric axes.
77985.explanation:
Steps to draw an isometric cube:

1. Draw the isometric axes at $30°$ to the horizontal.
2. Mark a point O as the origin.
3. From O, measure $50 \text{ mm}$ along each axis to locate points A, B, and C.
4. Complete the top face by drawing lines parallel to the axes.
5. From the vertices of the top face, draw vertical lines downward (isometric height) to complete the cube.

77986.subject: Technical Drawing
77986.question_text: State five fundamental principles of dimensioning in Technical Drawing and explain why each is important.
77986.explanation:
The five fundamental principles of dimensioning are:

1. Clarity: Dimensions should be clear and unambiguous to avoid misinterpretation.
2. Completeness: All necessary dimensions must be provided to fully define the object.
3. Non-duplication: Avoid repeating dimensions to prevent confusion.
4. Avoidance of hidden lines: Dimensions should not be placed on hidden lines.
5. Chain dimensioning: Avoid long chains of dimensions; use datum dimensioning where possible for accuracy.
